acceptanceCriteria: A fixed sequence [120, 20, 22, 21] proves the first process call is classified as cold; grouping into cold/warm happens on the original call order before any sorting, and a regression test pins this behavior.
Cold and warm raw sample lists preserve original call order in the output; percentiles are computed only from a separately sorted copy, and the quantile method is recorded.
p50/p95 are withheld with an explicit insufficient_samples reason below defined reliability floors instead of reporting a misleading percentile from too few samples.
regression_gate.sh accepts real non-integer elapsedMs/maxElapsedMs values without weakening identity mismatch or budget-exceeded failure detection; its existing self-test continues to pass.

Each capture records environment metadata (hardware, OS, filesystem, runtime identity, repository head/branch/dirty state, tracked file count) and discloses pre-measurement identity-probe invocations so no sample is misrepresented as a true OS-cold-cache call.
cargo fmt, cargo clippy, cargo test --workspace, and tests/performance/regression_gate_test.sh continue to pass; no governance decision or evidence semantics change.
goal: Establish a trustworthy development performance baseline harness: preserve original sample call order for cold/warm grouping, withhold unreliable percentile claims, disclose pre-measurement identity-probe warm-up, record measurement environment, and let regression_gate.sh consume real (non-integer) elapsed measurements.
intent: Fix the cold/warm sample misclassification defect in the local development performance benchmark harness (tests/performance/runtime_benchmark.sh): it sorts all samples before selecting the minimum as cold, which silently swaps the first process call for whichever later call happens to be fastest. Make cold/warm grouping, quantile reliability, and environment disclosure trustworthy before any runtime optimization work proceeds.
